newsitem.title: UK: Snakeboard sets AIM debut premium.
newsitem.headline: Snakeboard sets AIM debut premium.

text.p: Shares in "X-Treme" sports specialist Snakeboard International Plc set a 25 percent premium as they snaked onto the London Stock Exchange's Alternative Investment Market (AIM) on Thursday.
By 0900 GMT the shares were marked up at 3-3/4p compared with their issue price of 3p, although no early trade was registered in the stock.

The company, set up by two South African-born entrepreneurs, Oliver Macleod-Smith and James Fisher, produces and distributes snakeboards, a kind of skateboard with twin platforms, four wheels and a pivoting axle. Sales were 2.2 million stg in the 10 months to March 1996.
The float, with Neill Clerk Capital as adviser and Ellis and Partners as broker, raised 3.0 million stg and valued the company at 30.0 million stg.
The proceeds will be used to develop the business.
